questions.q: What problem does a description rule solve?
options: It prevents journal entries from being unbalanced
It builds a dynamic, transaction-specific description for each journal line instead of a generic, repeated label
It decides which GL account a line posts to
It merges duplicate journal lines together
questions.explain: Without a description rule, lines can default to a generic label repeated across every transaction; a description rule makes each line's text specific to that transaction.

questions.q: What two kinds of elements does a description rule combine to build its text?
options: Only mapping sets
Constant text and sources (transaction data such as supplier name or invoice number)
Only account rules
Only journal line types
questions.explain: A description rule concatenates fixed constant text with sources pulled from the transaction to build a specific, readable description.

questions.q: In the worked example, what did the improved description rule for a Payables invoice line produce?
options: A blank description
The same generic text as before, "Invoice"
A specific description combining the constant "Invoice", the supplier name, and the invoice number
Only the invoice amount with no other text
questions.explain: The improved rule combined constant text with supplier name and invoice number sources to produce something like "Invoice: Acme Office Supply : INV-48213."

questions.q: Why does a well-built description rule matter for later activities in this course, like reconciliation and audit?
options: It has no real effect on reconciliation or audit work
Specific, meaningful descriptions make it faster and less error-prone to read reports like the Account Analysis Report without opening every transaction
Descriptions are only visible to system administrators, not auditors
It replaces the need for account rules entirely
questions.explain: Clear, transaction-specific descriptions speed up reading subledger reports and reduce the need to drill into individual transactions during reconciliation or audit.

questions.q: Does the same description rule produce identical text for every transaction it runs against?
options: Yes, description rules always produce exactly the same text for every transaction
No, because the rule pulls from sources, the resulting text is specific to each transaction's actual data
Description rules cannot use any transaction data at all
Only Receivables transactions can use description rules
questions.explain: Because sources reflect each transaction's own data, the same description rule produces different, transaction-specific text for each event it processes.
